name: Motorcycle
description: A road motor vehicle steered by handlebars, with a seat the rider sits astride and no more than three wheels on the ground. An electric one is a motorcycle rather than a low-power scooter when its motor exceeds 4,476 watts or it has a manual clutch. Defined by Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(55), with HB 26-1079 (2026) adding parental permission for a minor's motorcycle permit.
restrictions: Handlebars connected to the front wheel or wheels, a seat the rider sits astride, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor exceeds 4,476 W or it has a manual clutch; below that, without a manual clutch, it is a low-power scooter
Built for the roadways; one designed primarily for use off the public highways, such as an electric dirt bike, is an off-highway vehicle instead
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement; a three-wheel-only endorsement doesn't cover a two-wheeler

The endorsement requires age 16; riders under 18 must first hold a motorcycle instruction permit for 12 months, and those under 16 must pass a Colorado State Patrol-approved training course before getting one
From August 12, 2026, a minor under 18 who isn't emancipated needs a parent's or legal guardian's written permission to get a motorcycle instruction permit (HB 26-1079)
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218
Riders and passengers must wear goggles or eyeglasses with safety glass or plastic lenses, unless their helmet has eye protection
Titled, registered and plated with the DMV, and must carry liability insurance
Entitled to a full traffic lane; no lane splitting, passing in the same lane, or riding more than two abreast
Restricted to roads and to OHV trails and forest roads open to motorized use; not allowed on sidewalks or non-motorized trails
On OHV trails and public-land routes, a plated motorcycle also needs a Colorado Parks and Wildlife OHV permit
